title: The molecular neuropathology of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: protocol for systematic review and meta-analysis
author: Elizabeth Elliott
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbnnimde

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Search for quantitative molecular studies of human ALS and ALS-FTD tissue compared to controls across specified databases using defined search terms.

substeps.instruction: Search PubMed using: ((“human” AND “post-mortem” OR “PM” OR “post mortem”)) AND (“ALS” or “MND”)
Search MEDLINE using: (human and (post-mortem or PM or post mortem) and (ALS or MND))
Search EMBASE using: (human and (post-mortem or PM or post mortem) and (ALS or MND))
Apply no restrictions on publication date or language (Search date: 07/06/2019)

steps.title: Screen Studies for Eligibility
steps.instruction: Screen titles and abstracts to identify studies meeting inclusion criteria and remove duplicates.

substeps.instruction: Use the Systematic Review Facility online screening tool (app.syrf.org.uk) with two independent authors
Resolve discordance (concordance <0.66) via consensus decision
Import selected studies to EndNote and discard duplicates
Include all quantitative molecular studies of human ALS neuropathological tissue compared to a control group (assess studies without control groups on an individual basis)
Exclude animal studies, reviews, letters, comments, case reports, and neuroimaging studies

steps.title: Assess Study Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the methodological quality of selected studies using an adapted CAMARADES' checklist.

substeps.instruction: One reviewer scores studies based on 8 items: 1) Peer reviewed publication, 2) Blinded assessments, 3) Sample size calculation, 4) Sample clinical and genetic profiling, 5) Statement of age/gender matched controls, 6) Statement regarding tissue quality (PMI, RIN, pH), 7) Appropriate statistical methods, 8) Statement of potential conflict of interest
Calculate the median number of checklist items scored and the interquartile range
Perform an independent review of 10% of selected studies to assess inter-observer variability

steps.title: Extract Study Data
steps.instruction: Extract specific study characteristics and outcome measures from the selected literature.

substeps.instruction: Extract citation info: author and year
Extract sample sizes for disease and controls
Extract clinical profiles: diagnosis and duration (ALS or ALS-FTD), genetic status of ALS samples, control profile (healthy, other), sex, and mean age
Extract molecular details: entity detected (DNA, mRNA, MiRNA, lncRNA, protein), quantification assay, outcome type/value, and regions assessed (BA or specific neuroanatomical regions)
Extract key findings, all outcome measures for patients and controls (increase/decrease value), and tissue quality markers (PMI, pH, RIN)

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the extracted quantitative data using standardized mean differences and meta-analysis models.

substeps.instruction: Calculate standardized mean differences (SMD) to enable inter-study comparison
Compare SMDs using Hedges’ g-statistic with a random effects model to account for small sample size bias
Report SMDs as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals
Assess heterogeneity using I2-values
Evaluate publication bias using a funnel plot and Egger’s regression test
